label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

Research notes (from 3 web searches):
Claim 0: Holland Tunnel 84 fans change all its air every 90 seconds. Supported as written.
- ASME landmark brochure: a total of 84 fans (42 blowers, 42 exhaust); at full speed they can completely change the tunnel air every 90 seconds. Source: https://www.asme.org/wwwasmeorg/media/ResourceFiles/AboutASME/Who We Are/Engineering History/Landmarks/93-Holland-Tunnel-Ventilation-System.pdf
- ETHW ASME landmark page: same. Source: https://ethw.org/ASME-Landmark:Holland_Tunnel_Ventilation_System
- Britannica Holland Tunnel: air changed every 90 seconds. Source: https://www.britannica.com/topic/Holland-Tunnel

Claim 1: Brunel shield; Thames Tunnel opened 1843, first tunnel under a navigable river. Supported as written.
- Wikipedia Thames Tunnel: first tunnel known to have been constructed successfully underneath a navigable river; opened 25 March 1843; built with Brunel and Cochrane tunnelling shield. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thames_Tunnel
- ASCE landmark: first shield-driven tunnel, first successful soft ground subaqueous tunnel. Source: https://www.asce.org/about-civil-engineering/history-and-heritage/historic-landmarks/thames-tunnel

Claim 2: a TBM lines the tunnel with rings of bolted curved segments as it goes. Supported in a corrected form: the lining is precast concrete segments set as successive rings by an erector at the rear of the shield, fastened by bolts or dowels.
- US patent 10472962: lining made of prefabricated segments arranged in successive rings, laid by an erector at the rear of the shield. Source: https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/10472962
- Crosscut (SR 99 tunnel): the erector arm sets each 16-ton liner segment in place. Source: https://crosscut.com/2013/07/going-deep-how-bore-tunnel-pictures
